S.FORM: ʔuuna=ku tia=kaari sua iisi ia, ma-naasə sumukun.
S.PHON: ʔuunaku tiakaari sua iiʂi ia manaasə sumukun
S.FORM: 'uunaku tiakaari sua iisi ia, manaase sumukun.
S.PHON: ʔuunaku tiakaa[r|ɾ]i sua iiʂi ia manaase sumukun
S.TRANSL: I have got perhaps a Bunun story.
It is based on Bunun.
Someone went to set traps in a mountain.
Four days later, he was returning to check the traps.
There was a cobra on the path.
It was right in the passage (to the traps).
It might bite.

S.FORM: mu-a-caa=kan caau iisa tia=maa-rakiau, ʔaisi mu-s-taruʔu vunai.
S.PHON: muaʦaakan ʦaau iisa tiamaarakiau ʔaiʂi mustaruʔu vunai
S.FORM: muacaakan caau iisa tiamaarakiau, 'aisi mustaru'u vunai.
S.PHON: muaʦaakan ʦaau iisa tiamaa[r|ɾ]akiau ʔaiʂi musta[r|ɾ]uʔu vunai
S.TRANSL: The person tried another path, but the snake was still blocking (the path).
The cobra would bite.
The person was in trouble.
It was daytime.
"What shall I do?" he said.
He saw the cobra still on the path.
Its neck stretched out.
It was going to fly at him and bite him.
The Bunun took up his gun and loaded it with bullets.
He took aim and shot at it.
The bullet pierced its neck.
The cobra died there.

S.FORM: makasua=cu sumukun iisua ma-naasə ʔaisi=cu ma-caŋ-caŋarə.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu sumukun iisua manaasə ʔaiʂiʦu maʦaŋʦaŋarə
makasuaʦu sumukun iisua manaase ʔaiʂiʦu maʦaŋʦaŋa[r|ɾ]e
S.TRANSL: The Bunun really felt relieved.
There was no more snake blocking him on the path.
He went to check the traps.
A goat was caught in a trap.
When he returned home, it was getting dark.

S.FORM: mu-usa-ini=kani ʔinia, mu-s-taru-taruʔu ʔinia ia, caʔania=pa=kani pu-aiʔ-ini.
S.PHON: muusainikani ʔinia mustarutaruʔu ʔinia ia ʦaʔaniapakani puaiʔini
muusainikani ʔinia musta[r|ɾ]uta[r|ɾ]uʔu ʔinia ia ʦaʔaniapakani puaiʔini
S.TRANSL: When he was going to (the mountain), it was still daytime.
He carried home the trapped goat.

S.PHON: paaʂiaikan ʔuʦaŋini misainkasu pakaruuruuvana kisaənkani ʔuʦaŋini
paaʂiaikan ʔuʦaŋini misainkasu paka[r|ɾ]uu[r|ɾ]uuvana kisaenkani ʔuʦaŋini
S.TRANSL: His wife talked to him, "Why are you here so late in the evening?"
"Because there was a snake blocking me (on the path)."

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.TRANSL: "What did you do to the snake?" his wife asked.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.TRANSL: "What did you do to the snake?" his wife asked.
"I shot it," the man replied.

S.FORM: ni-panaʔə=kani=kiai suma-kusa na əʔər-ini suma-nalusu, suma-nalusu=kani na ukuca-ini.
S.PHON: nipanaʔəkanikiai sumakusa na əʔərini sumanaɾusu sumanaɾusukani na ukuʦaini
S.FORM: nipana'ekanikiai sumakusa na e'erini sumanarusu, sumanarusukani na ukucaini.
S.PHON: nipanaʔekanikiai sumakusa na eʔe[r|ɾ]ini sumana[r|ɾ]usu sumana[r|ɾ]usukani na ukuʦaini
S.TRANSL: He shot it and (the bullet) pierced it's neck and came out it's back.

S.FORM: makasua=cu ʔulai=kani ʔinia takuisi, su-avuŋ=kani na=mu-liuŋuu taanaasa-ini.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu ʔuɾaikani ʔinia takuiʂi suavuŋkani namuɾiuŋuu taanaasaini
makasuaʦu ʔu[r|ɾ]aikani ʔinia takuiʂi suavuŋkani namu[r|ɾ]iuŋuu taanaasaini
S.TRANSL: They cut the goat into small pieces and shared them with their neighbors.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.FORM: araanai ʔinia sua ni-m-panaʔə iisua mu-sukuamə, mu-sukuam=kani tu-pau sua əʔər-ini.
S.PHON: araanai ʔinia sua nimpanaʔə iisua musukuamə musukuamkani tupau sua əʔərini
S.FORM: araanai 'inia sua nimpana'e iisua musukuame, musukuamkani tupau sua e'erini.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]aanai ʔinia sua nimpanaʔe iisua musukuame musukuamkani tupau sua eʔe[r|ɾ]ini
S.TRANSL: Since then the man who shot the snake became sick with a hole in his neck.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.FORM: araanai ʔinia sua ni-m-panaʔə iisua mu-sukuamə, mu-sukuam=kani tu-pau=kani sua əʔər-ini.
S.PHON: araanai ʔinia sua nimpanaʔə iisua musukuamə musukuamkani tupaukani sua əʔərini
S.FORM: araanai 'inia sua nimpana'e iisua musukuame, musukuamkani tupaukani sua e'erini.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]aanai ʔinia sua nimpanaʔe iisua musukuame musukuamkani tupaukani sua eʔe[r|ɾ]ini
S.TRANSL: Since then the man who shot the snake became sick with a hole in his neck.
The lead (bullet) came out of its neck when he shot the cobra.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.TRANSL: The man died in that way.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.TRANSL: The man died in that way.

S.FORM: iimu kisa-i ma-maraŋ miana ia, "ʔakuni=ʔai t<um>ani-ulaʔə kulai" misa.
S.PHON: iimu kisai mamaraŋ miana ia ʔakuniʔai tumaniuɾaʔə kuɾai misa
S.FORM: iimu kisai mamarang miana ia, "'akuni'ai t<um>aniura'e kurai" misa.
S.PHON: iimu kisai mama[r|ɾ]aŋ miana ia ʔakuniʔai tumaniu[r|ɾ]aʔe ku[r|ɾ]ai misa
S.TRANSL: Therefore, elders in the past said, "Don't abuse any snake!"

S.FORM: nakai sua ma-manu taa-tiʔiŋ mamisa ia, kaʔan=cu taavalaʔə m-aku-aʔərə.
S.PHON: nakai sua mamanu taatiʔiŋ mamisa ia kaʔanʦu taavaɾaʔə makuaʔərə
S.FORM: nakai sua mamanu taati'ing mamisa ia, ka'ancu taavara'e makua'ere.
S.PHON: nakai sua mamanu taatiʔiŋ mamisa ia kaʔanʦu taava[r|ɾ]aʔe makuaʔe[r|ɾ]e
S.TRANSL: But nowadays young people will not listen even when we scold them.
(Even when we) tell them, "There is a snake", (they may not listen).

S.FORM: ma-manu taa-tiʔiŋ c<um>əʔəra-in ia, pati-saaʔə=kiai, əm-əsəʔə na pooti, um-avici taanaasa.
S.PHON: mamanu taatiʔiŋ ʦuməʔərain ia patisaaʔəkiai əməsəʔə na pooti umavitʂi taanaasa
S.FORM: mamanu taati'ing c<um>e'erain ia, patisaa'ekiai, emese'e na pooti, umavici taanaasa.
S.PHON: mamanu taatiʔiŋ ʦumeʔe[r|ɾ]ain ia patisaaʔekiai emeseʔe na pooti umavitʂi taanaasa
S.TRANSL: When young people see one, they will catch it, put it into a bag, and bring it home.

S.FORM: sua iiku ia, ʔapacuaʔ-ai c<um>əʔəra=ku vunai ia, kaʔan=ku t<um>a-tani-ulaʔə.
S.PHON: sua iiku ia ʔapaʦuaʔai ʦuməʔəraku vunai ia kaʔanku tumataniuɾaʔə
S.FORM: sua iiku ia, 'apacua'ai c<um>e'eraku vunai ia, ka'anku t<um>ataniura'e.
S.PHON: sua iiku ia ʔapaʦuaʔai ʦumeʔe[r|ɾ]aku vunai ia kaʔanku tumataniu[r|ɾ]aʔe
S.TRANSL: As for me, even when I see a snake, I won't abuse it.

S.FORM: si araanai na taamu kisa-i ma-maraŋ miana.
S.PHON: ʂi araanai na taamu kisai mamaraŋ miana
S.FORM: si araanai na taamu kisai mamarang miana.
S.PHON: ʂi a[r|ɾ]aanai na taamu kisai mama[r|ɾ]aŋ miana
S.TRANSL: Elders in the past referred to a hundred pacer (type of snake).
Hey, (if we) see a hundred pacer, it is something different.
I shall talk about this later.
It is just like that.
That is all that I can tell you.
Stay healthy!
Thank you.
